messages.author: 67d9969f93ac5614
messages.subject: How to change colour mapping of the fill aesthetic into greyscales?
parts:
Dear all,

The following gives a nice bar plot:
* in qplot syntax:
qplot (x1, y, data=myData, fill=x2, geom="bar").
* in ggplot syntax:
b <- ggplot(myData)
b <- b + geom_bar( aes(x=x1, y=y, fill=x2) )
print(b)

x1 is mapped onto the x-axis, y is mapped onto the y-axis and x2 is
mapped into bar segments with a particular colour. See figure in
attach (but ignore the faceting, that's not important here.)

Now I want to change one little thing: I do not want to have colours,
but would prefer grey shades. How can I bring about this change?

Many thanks for your help,

Adi

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: How to change colour mapping of the fill aesthetic into greyscales?

b+ scale_color_grey() + theme_bw()

http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_grey.html

Not sure if there is a difference with discrete/continuous variables
like other scales though.

Brandon

Dear Brandon,

Thanks for your reply and sorry for my late answer.

#fill with greyscale

This works.

But this doesn't. I get the error message "Error: could not find function "theme_bw"".
 
  more often than not it's an out of date R or ggplot2 that is the culprit. 

I installed ggplot2 through the "install.packages()" command (and did so just some weeks ago), so I guess that should be fairly recent. Which other packages of R should i check?


Thanks for your help!

 
Aditya

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: How to change colour mapping of the fill aesthetic into greyscales?
parts:
Aditya,

theme_bw() should work. I use it regularly to make plots look a bit more like they do in publications. It eliminates the grey background, which may make it hard to read some of your bars (since invariably one of them will be of a similar shade of grey as the background).
> qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color)+scale_fill_grey()
> ggsave("greyscale.fill.png", width=4, height=4)
> qplot(cut, data=diamonds, geom="bar",fill=color)+scale_fill_grey()+theme_bw()

> ggsave("greyscale.fill.themeBW.png", width=4, height=4)
> 
I get no errors. 

Brandon
